[Center for Reservoir and Aquatic Systems Research (CRASR) · Baylor University]{.eyebrow}

[From field sensor to model]{.hero-title}

[This is the data science side of the Center for Reservoir and Aquatic Systems Research: the pipelines, databases, and statistical models that turn CRASR's monitoring of reservoirs and streams into data people can use.]{.hero-lead}

::: {.grid .pillars .column-page}
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .pillar}
#### Data infrastructure
Ingestion and QA/QC pipelines for lab instruments and field loggers, sample databases, and automated reports.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .pillar}
#### Statistical modeling
Hierarchical Bayesian models (Stan/brms) of water chemistry, decomposition, and reservoir response to drought.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .pillar}
#### Open tools
R packages, desktop tools, and reusable workflows, shared openly where we can. [See tools →](projects.qmd#category=Tools)
:::
:::

::: {.ai-band .column-page}
#### How we use AI
We aim to use generative AI openly: people stay accountable for the work, every substantive use is disclosed by research stage along with how it was checked, and a short log lives with the code. Our policy, a drop-in template, and an R helper are public for anyone to adopt.

[Read the policy](projects/ai-use.qmd){.btn .btn-green}
[CRASR/ai-use on GitHub](https://github.com/CRASR/ai-use){.btn .btn-outline-green}
:::
